- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days), then gradually underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in true values — model reacts too quickly to recent highs.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates the “tail” of the trend.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the middle of the forecast — it holds onto upward momentum longer than observed.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent history, especially the last 5–7 days, leading to overfitting to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of upward trends in the final 10–15 days, particularly when true values show accelerating growth.
- Model tends to underestimate the “recovery” phase after a dip — it doesn’t fully account for rebounding momentum.
- Forecasts are often too smooth — they miss abrupt, high-impact price jumps that occur in the last 3–5 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits a lag in recognizing sustained upward momentum — it takes 2–3 days to adjust to a new trend direction.
- Model overreacts to minor price corrections — it underestimates the “reversal” effect after a spike, leading to premature downward forecasts.
